mcp_detail: MCP server documented at https://developer.brex.com/docs/mcp and listed in the Model Context Protocol registry (search=brex).
primary_blocker: Requires admin approval to obtain API tokens

REST API documented on the developer portal.
MCP server is mentioned in vendor docs and listed in the MCP registry.
API is documented and usable once credentials are obtained, but requires admin approval.

description: PitchBook provides a data API accessed via an API key, obtainable through a self‑serve free trial sign‑up. No public MCP or community registry entry exists, and the official documentation does not expose a public REST or GraphQL endpoint beyond the trial portal.

description: NotebookLM is an enterprise extension of Google Gemini, exposing a REST API for notebook management. Developers authenticate via OAuth2 (Google Cloud IAM) or API keys in the developer API, and can obtain free trial credentials for 14 days. The API is narrowly scoped to notebook operations and is officially documented on Google Cloud’s site.
mcp_detail: Community MCPs exist at dev.cotlet/notebooklm and io.github.Pantheon-Security/notebooklm-mcp-secure, but no official Google MCP.

evidence.claim: API key mentioned in Gemini developer API

notes: The documentation indicates a self‑serve trial but the product is marketed as Enterprise, so usage in production may require an enterprise agreement.

description: Reducto is a document parsing platform offering a REST API for developers to process various file types. Access appears to be gated, with indications of partner or enterprise-level onboarding and pricing. The API is documented and supports OAuth2 and API Key authentication. No publicly available free trial or sandbox is confirmed, and MCP server documentation is present but not listed in the official registry.
mcp_detail: MCP server docs mentioned but not listed in official registry

description: Devin offers a REST API for interacting with its AI services, primarily designed for enterprise customers. Authentication is through API keys or Personal Access Tokens, both of which are gated behind enterprise approval or admin approval workflows. The API is documented and accessible via HTTPS, but requires a paid enterprise subscription or administrator approval. Devin also publishes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface for DeepWiki integration, available in the public MCP registry and as a Composio toolkit.
mcp_detail: Devin’s DeepWiki MCP is listed in the public MCP registry (io.devinbox/devinbox) and available as a community‑developed Composio toolkit.

evidence.claim: Authentication via API Key and Personal Access Token
Requires enterprise approval/admin approval for PATs; API keys available for enterprise users
MCP documented and present in public registry

notes: The documentation indicates that API keys and PATs are tied to enterprise or organization accounts, implying a paid or approved plan is necessary. No free tier or sandbox is mentioned.

MCP functionality is referenced in Grain docs but is implemented only by third‑party community packages.
